title: verify_smime_signer / verify_smime_recipient distinction is documentation-only — no shipped profile enforces it
description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:930-1028: verify_smime_signer and verify_smime_recipient have BYTE-IDENTICAL function bodies. The rustdoc at line 939-942 says 'The signer-vs-recipient distinction is encoded in the caller-supplied Profile's ValidationPolicy: signer profiles require KeyUsage digitalSignature, recipient profiles require keyEncipherment.' But pkix-profiles ships only BasicSmimeProfile, which sets required_leaf_eku=emailProtection and require_rfc822_san=true — it does NOT set any KU requirement. There is no BasicSmimeSignerProfile / BasicSmimeRecipientProfile. So in practice both wrappers do the same thing for the only shipped profile. Trigger: caller writes verify_smime_recipient(signer_cert_chain, ...) expecting recipient-shape enforcement, gets exactly what verify_smime_signer would have returned, including for a cert with KU=digitalSignature only. Documentation promises a guarantee that the shipped profile does not deliver. Two options: (1) ship BasicSmimeSignerProfile/BasicSmimeRecipientProfile with the documented KU shapes, OR (2) reword the rustdoc to be honest that the distinction is intent-only and the caller must wire a profile that imposes the KU constraint they want. Recommend option (1) so new callers don't have to read this footnote.
notes:
Analysis 2026-11-25: bead confirmed and WORSE than filed. The documentation half is fixed (commit follows); the feature half is scoped below. P1 -> P2 because nothing now lies and no caller is misled.

Verified both claims. The bodies ARE byte-identical -- my first diff said otherwise and was misaligned; reading both in full confirms the bead. And BasicSmimeProfile sets only required_leaf_eku = emailProtection and require_rfc822_san = true, with no KU requirement.

Worse than filed: the bead frames this as "pkix-profiles ships only BasicSmimeProfile ... there is no BasicSmimeSignerProfile / BasicSmimeRecipientProfile", i.e. a missing profile. The real situation is that no profile COULD express it. pkix_path::ValidationPolicy has NO field for a required leaf KeyUsage. enforce_key_usage is about keyCertSign on INTERMEDIATES (RFC 5280 6.1.4(n), per its own rustdoc), and grepping pkix-path for digital_signature / key_encipherment outside comments returns nothing -- leaf key usage is not checked anywhere. So the rustdoc was not describing an unshipped profile, it was describing a mechanism that does not exist.

Done now (option 2, reworded honestly): both wrappers state plainly that the distinction is not enforced and the bodies are identical, say why ValidationPolicy cannot express it, and tell a caller to check the leaf KeyUsage themselves. Put on BOTH functions, since someone reading only the recipient one should not have to find the signer one to learn this.

Scoped for option 1, if you want the real thing. Three parts:
1. Add a required-leaf-KU field to ValidationPolicy. It is #[non_exhaustive], so additive and non-breaking.
2. Enforce it on the leaf in pkix-path. This is new validation logic, not a wiring change.
3. Ship BasicSmimeSignerProfile and BasicSmimeRecipientProfile in pkix-profiles.

Design constraint that must not be missed: the recipient side is NOT a single bit. RFC 8551 4.4.2 covers both RSA key transport (keyEncipherment) and key agreement (keyAgreement), so the field needs ANY-OF semantics, not all-of. A recipient profile requiring keyEncipherment alone -- which is literally what the old rustdoc promised -- would reject every ECDH recipient. Confirmed concrete, not hypothetical: the sibling smime-tree crate decrypts EnvelopedData with RSA PKCS#1v15 AND ECDH P-256/P-384, so a keyEncipherment-only recipient profile would break half of our own S/MIME stack.

Signer side is also two bits: RFC 8551 accepts digitalSignature or nonRepudiation.
